results.name: A guest with 0 XP does not appear on the leaderboard (honestly excluded, not a zero-score entry)
After earning real XP, the guest appears with the correct server-side xpTotal (not client-submitted)
isCurrentUser is computed server-side by matching the verified identity cookie, never client-supplied
Both tied learners appear on the board with the same xpTotal
An exact tie (same XP, same completed-session count) breaks deterministically by guest_reference ASC
Re-earning the same named XP source a second time does not inflate the total (server-side one-time enforcement)
An ordinary (non-staff) identity cannot invoke a correction
A staff-authorized XP correction succeeds
The corrected xpTotal is applied immediately (server-authoritative recalculation, not a cached snapshot)
The corrected guest no longer appears on the leaderboard (0 XP is honestly excluded — placement genuinely recalculated, not just relabeled)
Before opting out, the guest is visible on the leaderboard
A guest can set their own eligible:false preference
After opting out, the guest no longer appears on the leaderboard (server-enforced, not a UI-only toggle)
A completely separate guest never has isCurrentUser incorrectly true for another guest's row
A guest can set their own venue scope
A venue-scoped query does not include a guest explicitly scoped to a different venue
The same venue-scoped query DOES include a guest explicitly scoped to that venue
Guest-to-account conversion succeeds
Conversion reports the leaderboard preference (opt-out + venue) was transferred (real found-and-fixed gap — was previously never transferred)
The opt-out preference carried over — the now-authenticated account still does not appear on the global leaderboard
Two independent live fetches under the same identity return identical server-authoritative xpTotal (no local mirror to desync)
Pagination returns real, non-overlapping pages via LIMIT/OFFSET
Page 2 entries do not duplicate page 1 entries (real SQL OFFSET, not a client-side re-slice of the same data)
A limit above the max (100) is server-side clamped, never trusting an arbitrarily large client-requested page size
A negative offset is server-side clamped to 0
